data.name: Torin1
data.description: ATP-competitive ('active-site') mTOR inhibitor. Unlike rapamycin, it blocks the kinase active site directly and so fully inhibits BOTH complexes - the tool that revealed rapamycin-resistant functions of mTORC1.
data.description_beginner: A lab-only drug that blocks mTOR directly at its 'engine room' (the active site), so - unlike rapamycin - it shuts down both mTOR complexes completely. It was a key tool for discovering what rapamycin-resistant mTOR functions look like.

studies.title: An ATP-competitive mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitor reveals rapamycin-resistant functions of mTORC1
studies.authors: Thoreen CC; Kang SA; Chang JW; Liu Q; Zhang Jianming; Gao Y; Reichling LJ; Sim T; Sabatini DM; Gray NS

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Dropped a bombshell: rapamycin does NOT fully block mTORC1. Using Torin1 (which jams the active site directly), the authors showed rapamycin leaves important mTORC1 jobs running - notably 4E-BP1 phosphorylation and autophagy suppression. This reframed a decade of rapamycin experiments and launched the search for complete inhibitors.

studies.title: mTORC1 phosphorylation sites encode their sensitivity to starvation and rapamycin
studies.authors: Kang SA; Pacold ME; Cervantes CL; Lim D; Lou HJ; Ottina K; Gray NS; Turk BE; Yaffe MB; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human and mouse cell lines; in vitro mTORC1 kinase assays on peptide substrates
studies.finding: Each mTORC1 phosphorylation site has its own intrinsic 'substrate quality'. Good substrates stay phosphorylated when mTORC1 is partly inhibited by rapamycin or starvation, poor ones drop out first, and changing a few residues around a site shifts its sensitivity in cells. One level of mTORC1 activity can therefore produce different output profiles.

studies.title: Lysosomal metabolomics reveals V-ATPase- and mTOR-dependent regulation of amino acid efflux from lysosomes
studies.authors: Abu-Remaileh M; Wyant GA; Kim C; Laqtom NN; Abbasi M; Chan SH; Freinkman E; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Turns the lysosome from a place where mTORC1 is switched on into something mTORC1 also controls: inhibiting mTOR strongly reduces the efflux of most essential amino acids out of the lysosome, so the organelle becomes a store rather than a source. Measured directly by rapidly isolating lysosomes and profiling their contents, which is why the claim is about concentrations inside the organelle and not inferred from signalling readouts. Boundary: one human cell line, acute pharmacological inhibition.

studies.title: ULK1 induces autophagy by phosphorylating Beclin-1 and activating VPS34 lipid kinase
studies.authors: Russell RC; Tian Y; Yuan H; Park HW; Chang YY; Kim J; Kim H; Neufeld TP; Dillin A; Guan KL

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Wild-type, ULK-deficient (ULK1-/- with ULK2 knockdown) and FIP200-/- MEFs; HEK293 and HeLa Beclin-1 knockdown-reconstitution lines; in vitro kinase assays with insect-cell ULK1/ULK2; C. elegans bec-1 S6A transgenic embryos
studies.finding: The authors asked how the ULK1 kinase switches on autophagy when amino acids are withdrawn. In mouse fibroblasts, amino-acid starvation raised the lipid-kinase activity of VPS34 complexes that contain ATG14L while lowering other VPS34 complexes, and the activation needed ULK kinase activity (lost in ULK-deficient and FIP200-null cells). ULK1 directly phosphorylated Beclin-1 at serine 14 (serine 15 in human), shown with purified kinase, mass spectrometry and a phospho-specific antibody; the mTOR inhibitor Torin1 or amino-acid withdrawal raised this phosphorylation only in cells with ULK activity. Cells reconstituted with non-phosphorylatable Beclin-1 S14A did not increase autophagosomes on amino-acid starvation, and the matching worm mutant (BEC-1 S6A) failed to fully rescue autophagic clearance in C. elegans embryos. The work provided evidence for a signalling chain from mTORC1 inhibition to ULK1, Beclin-1 and the ATG14L-VPS34 complex. Boundary: Mouse and human cell lines, in vitro kinase assays and C. elegans embryos; the mTOR step relies on Torin1 (which blocks mTORC1 and mTORC2) and amino-acid withdrawal. Not tested in mammalian tissues or in people.

studies.title: Rag GTPases mediate amino acid-dependent recruitment of TFEB and MITF to lysosomes

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human ARPE-19, HeLa, HEK-293T cells; siRNA against Raptor, RagA/B, RagC/D, p18 (LAMTOR1); active/inactive Rag mutants; TFEB and MITF deletion/point mutants; Torin1 and amino-acid starvation
studies.finding: The authors asked how TFEB reaches the lysosome, where mTORC1 phosphorylates it. In human cells, depleting Raptor inactivated mTORC1 and sent TFEB to the nucleus but did not stop TFEB binding lysosomes (82.5% of cells still showed lysosomal TFEB), whereas depleting the Rag GTPases or the Ragulator subunit p18 abolished it (under 4% of Rag-depleted cells kept the S211A mutant on lysosomes, against about 80% of controls). TFEB bound only active Rag heterodimers through its first 30 amino acids, and active Rags were enough to bring TFEB to lysosomes; TFEB mutants that could not bind Rags lost S211 phosphorylation and stayed in the nucleus. Endogenous TFEB accumulated in the nucleus after Torin1 or amino-acid starvation and moved back to the cytosol and lysosomes when amino acids were added again. Some MITF isoforms behaved the same way. Boundary: Human cell lines, mostly with overexpressed or mutant proteins; not tested in tissues or whole animals.

studies.title: NUFIP1 is a ribosome receptor for starvation-induced ribophagy
studies.authors: Wyant GA; Abu-Remaileh M; Frenkel EM; Laqtom NN; Dharamdasani V; Lewis CA; Chan SH; Heinze I; Ori A; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: HEK-293T and other human/mouse cell lines (incl. 8988T); LysoIP lysosome proteomics; CRISPR knockouts of NUFIP1, ATG7, DEPDC5 (GATOR1); Torin1, amino-acid and glucose starvation; electron microscopy
studies.finding: The authors purified lysosomes from human cells and measured how their protein content changes when mTORC1 is switched off by nutrient starvation or by the mTOR inhibitor Torin1, defining 828 lysosome-associated proteins. One responder, NUFIP1 (with its partner ZNHIT3), moved from the nucleus to autophagosomes and lysosomes after mTORC1 inhibition, bound ribosomes from Torin1-treated cells, and bound LC3B directly through a motif lost in the W40A mutant. Without NUFIP1 or its LC3B-binding ability, starvation or Torin1 no longer depleted ribosomal proteins and rRNA, while bulk autophagy and ferritin degradation were unaffected. In cells lacking the GATOR1 subunit DEPDC5, where mTORC1 ignores amino-acid loss, starvation no longer depleted ribosomal proteins but Torin1 still did, which points to mTORC1 inhibition as the trigger. NUFIP1 loss reduced survival under starvation (rescued by nucleosides) and blunted mTORC1 reactivation after long arginine deprivation. Boundary: Human and mouse cell lines over hours of starvation; Torin1 inhibits both mTOR complexes. No tissue or whole-animal data.
